transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-31
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Solutions Eng); Rajiv Menon (NovaHealth - Head of ML), Elena Gomez (Platform), Chris Liu (Security)

Summary:
Quick migration/demo focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together APIs to Redwood. Showed Redwood API equivalents for chat/completions, embeddings, streaming and function calling, and discussed Dedicated vs Hosted, VPC/private deployment, security (SOC2/KMS/SAML), and benchmarking next steps.

Topics: parity mapping, token costs, model variants, latency SLOs, KV cache/batching, private deployment, security docs, pilot scope

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy new years eve, we will try to keep it tight. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Daniel and Lena.
[00:07] Rajiv Menon: Thanks, yeah appreciate you doing this on short notice, trying to lock down migration plan before the holiday break.
[00:12] Daniel Park: Cool. We'll walk through a parity mapping — basically: you call Redwood the same way you do OpenAI/Anthropic/Together, but with a few parameter differences and a couple of feature names. We'll show the API, Console, and Optimize tips for cost/latency.
[00:25] Elena Gomez: The main ask from our side is feature parity for streaming + function calls, embeddings, and that the latency for our real-time assistant stays below 350ms P95. Also security, obviously.
[00:36] Chris Liu: And SOC2 plus KMS integration; we can't have prompt logs stored unencrypted in vendor cloud unless we control the keys.
[00:44] Maya Chen: Totally. We'll cover KMS and VPC options. Quick agenda: API parity examples, Console walkthrough, model recommendations with Redwood Optimize, and then Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:53] Rajiv Menon: Yep.
[00:55] [01:10] Daniel Park: Alright demo starts — here's a quick snippet: OpenAI chat call typically hits /v1/chat/completions. On Redwood it's /v1/generate or /v1/chat depending on whether you want structured tool calling; the SDKs map chat->chat, completions->generate. The payloads are similar: messages array, model string, temperature, max_tokens. Small differences: Redwood uses model aliasing and supports model variants via ?variant=quant or throughput variants, and we surface kv_cache_options and batching hints in the request meta.
[01:35] Rajiv Menon: kv_cache_options, can you explain, we currently rely on the OpenAI token cache to avoid repeated context cost for long conversations.
[01:42] Lena Ortiz: Yeah so Redwood has prefix/KV cache for conversation state; you can pin keys to tenant scope. In practice for your assistant we can cache the 1st 2-3 user turns; that reduces per-token compute and latency on hot paths.
[01:52] Elena Gomez: Sounds good. Is that automatic? We don't want to refactor prompts.
[01:55] Daniel Park: It's mostly automatic. You opt into caching and provide a cache key; the SDKs handle the rest. There's also a Console toggle to warm caches for canary testing.
[02:06] Chris Liu: About streaming and function calling — we use streaming with partial tokens and function calls to hit our retrieval system. Does Redwood support function call schema and streaming tokens?
[02:14] Daniel Park: Yes. Function calling is supported; we map it to Redwood's tool schema. Streaming uses SSE or websockets; payloads stream chunked tokens and function call events. We demo that'll in a sec.
[02:24] [03:00] Daniel Park (screen share): Opening Console -> API Explorer. Here I have a parity mapping doc open: column A is OpenAI parameter, column B is Redwood equivalent. Example: OpenAI's model 'gpt-4o' -> Redwood curated 'rwd-gpt4o-v1' (or use rwd-gpt4o-v1-quant for int8). temperature, top_p map 1:1. OpenAI max_tokens -> Redwood max_output_tokens. role: system/user -> same. function_call: 'auto'/'none' -> same.
[03:25] Rajiv Menon: What about embeddings? We use Anthropic for embeddings currently, and Together for a couple of cheaper models. How's parity there?
[03:33] Maya Chen: Redwood supports embeddings as a separate endpoint /v1/embeddings, same payload as others: model + input. We maintain a catalog. Example mapping: Anthropic-embed-x -> rwd-embed-1. We also have recommendations via Optimize which will suggest quantized embed models for high volume.
[03:48] Elena Gomez: Any differences in similarity cosine scaling or vector norms? We normalize on our side but want to make sure embeddings are comparable.
[03:55] Daniel Park: Embeddings vector length and norms are model-specific; we include a model card in the Console with expected vector dimensions and suggested normalization. Part of the parity doc is a mapping table and a small note on normalization differences — we'll send that.
[04:07] [05:20] Rajiv Menon: Cost question: Together and Anthropic are cheaper for embeddings per unit for our volume. If we switch to Redwood hosted, how do costs compare?
[04:30] Maya Chen: Short answer: depends on model and whether you use Dedicated. Redwood hosted pricing can be similar to or lower than Anthropic at scale due to batching and KV caching. Optimize will recommend batch sizes and quantized variants to reduce per-token cost. For strict per-call price comparisons we'll produce an estimated cost-delta spreadsheet.
[04:44] Chris Liu: If we go Dedicated or Private, how does billing work? We need an on-prem feel for compliance.
[04:50] Maya Chen: Dedicated is reserved capacity — monthly commit; Private is customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package. In Private we support BYOK and KMS/HSM. Billing can be consumption-based or committed with a platform fee. We'll include those options in the pricing doc.
[05:05] [06:00] Daniel Park: Now demo function calling + streaming: I'm going to call a Redwood chat endpoint with a function schema for their retrieval API. Watch the events: token chunks -> function_call.start -> function_call.args (streamed) -> function_call.end.
[06:15] [06:30] (audio glitch) Speaker 2: sorry small audio blip
[06:35] Daniel Park: ...and you can see partial responses arrive immediately. That helps hit your sub-350ms P95 for short replies because you can begin rendering partial tokens while the backend finishes.
[06:48] Elena Gomez: Is there a latency penalty for quantized models?
[06:52] Daniel Park: Usually quantized int8 models trade a small accuracy delta for 20-40% improved throughput and lower memory. For short-turn assistants, sometimes the CPU->GPU transfer or kernel path gives lower latency on certain hardware; Optimize helps pick best variant per workload.
[07:05] Rajiv Menon: On the topic of hardware, we run in GCP; what regions/hardware does Redwood support for Hosted and Dedicated?
[07:12] Lena Ortiz: Hosted covers major regions in us-east/us-west/eu-west; Dedicated can be colocated in GCP/AWS region of your choice as a managed private pool. For Private on-prem, we provide deployment artifacts and a support engagement.
[07:25] Chris Liu: For security: SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs — do you expose the raw transcript and who can access it?
[07:32] Maya Chen: Audit logs are available in Console and via API; access is RBAC controlled. For Private/Dedicated you can configure log forwarding to your SIEM and use KMS so Redwood never sees plaintext. For Hosted, we offer customer-managed keys for encryption at rest.
[07:46] [09:00] Elena Gomez: Any gotchas with rate limits when migrating from OpenAI? Our infra currently assumes X req/s and a few long-lived streams.
[08:00] Daniel Park: We can mirror your current rate/intensity in a benchmark. Redwood supports continuous batching; we recommend setting burst limits and configuring autoscaling policies for Dedicated. For Hosted we can set per-token quotas and per-route SLOs. We'll run a load test to verify.
[08:20] Rajiv Menon: Can you do a side-by-side of error modes? OpenAI sometimes returns incomplete function args or 429s under load.
[08:29] Daniel Park: Yes — Redwood has automatic fallback policies: if a model variant is out of capacity, requests route to a compatible variant. We log fallbacks. For incomplete function args, streaming helps because the function_call events are explicit; but network flakiness can still truncate streams — the SDK has retry semantics.
[08:50] [10:00] Daniel Park (screen share - Console -> Optimize): Here's Optimize — it analyzes usage patterns and gives recommendations: batch_size hints, model quantization suggestions, suggestion to enable KV cache for mid-length conversations, and a predicted cost impact. We can run Optimize against your sample logs or simulate using our benchmark harness.
[10:20] Rajiv Menon: How invasive is instrumentation? We want minimal changes to client code.
[10:25] Lena Ortiz: Most customers swap base endpoints and tweak a few params. If you use OpenAI SDKs, our SDK layer is a drop-in replacement in many languages. For Anthropic/Together differences we map role naming and some param names with a small compatibility shim.
[10:38] Elena Gomez: Are there SDKs for Java/Go/Python/Node?
[10:40] Maya Chen: Yes, official SDKs for Node/Python/Go/Java, and a CLI. We'll share quickstart snippets.
[10:47] [12:00] Chris Liu: About data residency — some of our PHI content must reside in EU. Does Redwood support region locking?
[12:08] Maya Chen: Yes, region pinning is available for Dedicated and hosted enterprise plans — you can pin workloads to eu-west. For Private, you control storage. We'll provide the compliance matrix.
[12:20] Rajiv Menon: For the pilot, we want to validate 3 things: parity of core APIs (chat/embeddings/function-calls), cost delta for our 50M token/mo workload, and latency under our traffic pattern. Can we scope a 4-week pilot?
[12:33] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Typical pilot: 2 weeks of benchmarking with your prompts + 2 weeks of small production traffic on Dedicated/Hosted evaluation. We'll propose a scope doc.
[12:44] [14:10] Daniel Park: Quick demo of model switching: in Console you can create a route that maps incoming model name to a Redwood model alias and set a fallback model. This is how you get minimal code changes — you keep referencing model names and the routing layer rewrites them.
[14:25] Elena Gomez: That routing layer — does it add hop/latency?
[14:28] Daniel Park: Negligible; it's a control plane decision. Runtime routing is optimized and collocated.
[14:34] [16:00] Rajiv Menon: Any customer references doing OpenAI->Redwood migration?
[16:05] Maya Chen: We have a case with a fintech and a healthcare analytics firm; I'll share redacted notes and a benchmark summary.
[16:12] Chris Liu: On the SOC2 and attestations — can you share last audit date and a copy of the report?
[16:17] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll attach the SOC2 report and our security whitepaper. For Private deployments we also provide SOC2 + penetration testing reports applicable to the package.
[16:26] [18:00] (minor crosstalk) Speaker 3: sorry —
[18:05] Elena Gomez: One more technical: our pipelines rely on embeddings produced with a specific seed / deterministic behavior. Are Redwood embeddings deterministic?
[18:12] Daniel Park: Embeddings are deterministic for a given model and input unless you enable sampling/noise. We'll document and run a deterministic test in the benchmark.
[18:22] Rajiv Menon: For the benchmark, do you need IAM creds or can you use a proxy?
[18:27] Maya Chen: We can set up a temporary test key scoped to your benchmark dataset; for Dedicated/Private we integrate with your IAM.
[18:33] [22:00] (demo continues, Daniel warms up a streaming function call)
[22:41] Daniel Park: Notice the function args stream in JSON chunks — SDK reassembles them client-side. If a chunk is missing due to network, there's a retry with the last event id.
[23:05] Rajiv Menon: Any known gotchas migrating from Together? Together uses a slightly different tokenization and we saw +2% token count.
[23:12] Daniel Park: Tokenization differences are real; Optimize will estimate effective token counts after mapping models. We can also add a pre-flight tokenizer check to estimate monthly token costs.
[23:25] [30:00] (planning and pricing discussion)
[30:10] Maya Chen: For your 50M token/month profile we will produce three scenarios: Hosted standard models, Hosted with quantized variants, and Dedicated reserved capacity. Each will include expected P95 latency, throughput, and monthly cost.
[30:26] Elena Gomez: Procurement question: What contract terms for Dedicated — minimum commitment length?
[30:32] Maya Chen: Typical is 12 months for Dedicated reserve; we can discuss a shorter pilot commitment. Private deployments have a platform fee + support. We'll have legal follow up.
[30:45] [35:00] Rajiv Menon: Are there SLA numbers for latency?
[35:07] Lena Ortiz: We publish uptime SLAs and latency targets for curated models under Dedicated. For Hosted we give SLO guidance and can offer SLA as an add-on. We'll include expected P95 in the pilot doc.
[35:20] Chris Liu: For logging and auditability — can we disable transcript retention entirely in Hosted?
[35:27] Maya Chen: You can disable storage of request bodies in hosted enterprise with data retention policies and customer-managed keys; otherwise deletions and retention windows apply. For Private you control retention.
[35:40] [40:00] (closing the demo)
[40:05] Maya Chen: Quick recap: we'll send parity mapping doc, cost scenario spreadsheet, SOC2 and security whitepaper, and propose a 4-week pilot scope. Daniel will run the benchmark once Chris sends the sample prompts.
[40:22] Rajiv Menon: Sounds good. Any blockers from your side?
[40:26] Daniel Park: None. We'll need the sample prompt set and a test key scope.
[40:30] Elena Gomez: I'll share the dataset and an infra contact to help with keys.
[40:34] Chris Liu: I'll review the security docs once you send, and provide KMS requirements.
[40:38] Maya Chen: Great — next steps and action items recorded, we'll follow up in email with attachments. Happy New Year and thanks.
[40:45] Rajiv Menon: Thanks everyone.
[40:47] (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional audio blips and some speaker mislabels around 06:30. We intentionally left a few shorthand terms (kv cache, rwd- model names) that may be transcribed loosely.
